questions.prompt: Explain why ParcelPilot stores the whole workspace as one aggregate and what 'available stock' means through a shipment's lifecycle.

keyPoints.text: A reservation creates a shipment and reduces stock for every selected item.
keyPoints.quote: A reservation creates a shipment and reduces available units for every selected item.

keyPoints.text: Saving those independently could leave a shipment without stock, or stock reduced without a shipment.
keyPoints.quote: Saving those changes independently could leave a shipment without reserved stock or reduce stock without a shipment.

keyPoints.text: The reducer works on a clone, so a rejection leaves accepted state untouched.
keyPoints.quote: If the fifth selected item is unavailable, the first four items in the accepted state must remain untouched.

keyPoints.text: Clamping negative stock would hide overselling.
keyPoints.quote: Clamping negative stock to zero would conceal overselling rather than prove that a reservation was possible.

keyPoints.text: Packing does not subtract again; shipping and delivery keep the deduction.
keyPoints.quote: Packing does not subtract again. Shipping and delivery retain the deduction.

keyPoints.text: Cancellation returns one per item and is terminal.
keyPoints.quote: Cancellation from Reserved or Packed returns one per item and becomes terminal, preventing a second return.

questions.prompt: Explain the two identities that prevent duplicates, and how snapshots separate history from current policy.

keyPoints.text: A request key identifies one attempted reservation; a matching retry returns the accepted shipment.
keyPoints.quote: Retrying it with the same fingerprint returns the accepted shipment.

keyPoints.text: Subscriber plus cycle month identifies the business slot, even after cancellation.
keyPoints.quote: A new request key cannot create another shipment for that same subscriber-month, even after cancellation.

keyPoints.text: Idempotency handles transport uncertainty; the cycle constraint enforces business policy.
keyPoints.quote: Idempotency handles transport uncertainty. The cycle constraint enforces the chosen business policy.

keyPoints.text: In SQL a preliminary lookup cannot arbitrate concurrent inserts.
keyPoints.quote: a preliminary lookup by itself cannot arbitrate concurrent inserts

keyPoints.text: Editing the live catalog must not change accepted shipment facts.
keyPoints.quote: Editing the live catalog later must not change those accepted facts.

keyPoints.text: Historical validation checks receipt consistency, not today's availability.
keyPoints.quote: Historical validation checks internal receipt consistency and references, not today's availability.

questions.prompt: Explain what the repository's concurrency control actually arbitrates, its costs, and why it is not security.

keyPoints.text: The check is optimistic concurrency on the entire workspace.
keyPoints.quote: So the check is optimistic concurrency on the **entire workspace**, not on the record being edited

keyPoints.text: In the last-unit race the loser is rejected by the baseline comparison before stock is consulted.
keyPoints.quote: the losing reservation is rejected by the baseline comparison ("Workspace changed in another tab") before `reduce` ever looks at stock

keyPoints.text: Two operators editing unrelated records conflict anyway.
keyPoints.quote: Two operators editing unrelated records conflict just the same.

keyPoints.text: Only reservations are idempotent, so a lost acknowledgement on other commands produces a misleading error.
It is a defensible choice for one operator but the first thing to change for shared workspaces.
keyPoints.quote: it is the first thing to change before several people share one workspace

keyPoints.text: None of this authenticates a user; devtools or scripts can bypass the repository.
keyPoints.quote: Developer tools or another script can bypass the repository.

keyPoints.text: A deployed app needs server identity, authorization, transactions and recovery.
keyPoints.quote: A deployed CRUD app needs server-side identity, authorization, database transactions, and operational recovery.
